## The theorem

**Theorem (two-invariant generation of the internal SM).** Let H_F be the finite internal space of D_IV⁵ and ∂_S its Shilov boundary. Define
- **I₁ = the reality-type census** of End_K(H_F): the assignment, to each K-isotypic block, of its Frobenius–Schur division algebra (ℝ, ℂ, or ℍ) and multiplicity — the datum (ℂ,1)⊕(ℍ,1)⊕(ℝ,3);
- **I₂ = the orientability class** of ∂_S = (S⁴×S¹)/ℤ₂: a single bit, *non-orientable* (Pin⁻, 𝒫² = −1).

Then every discrete/structural fact of the internal Standard Model is a function of (I₁, I₂), and:
- **(necessity)** neither is derivable from the other — I₁ is a representation-type datum, I₂ is a boundary-topology datum; dropping either loses facts (below);
- **(sufficiency)** together they reach *every* internal structural fact;
- **(minimality)** exactly two; there is no third generator, and neither is redundant.

| **no internal color group** (SU(3) not in the geometry) | **I₁ + Coleman–Mandula** | the ℝ block gives an SO(3) *rotation of physical directions* — a spacetime symmetry (T265: internal ⊥ spacetime), so it contributes **zero** internal generators |

| **custodial SU(2) / ρ ≈ 1 / no W_R** | **I₁** | the real SO(5) vector branches to a (2,2) bi-doublet under SO(4) (T2520) |
| **parity violation** (the world is left-handed at all) | **I₂** | a non-orientable (Pin⁻) boundary *permits* chirality; an orientable one would force vector-like (Witten no-go) |

The two "∧" rows are the reconciliation the promotion test forced: chirality and the Majorana neutrino were previously attributed to one cause each; they are in fact the **conjunction** of both invariants — I₂ opens the door, I₁ chooses who walks through.

## The readability criteria (why the negatives are predicted)

- **I₁ (Elie's criterion):** a fact is readable off the reality-type census **iff it is a class function on 𝕂 = {ℝ, ℂ, ℍ}** — constant on reality-type classes. Gauge dimension, chirality-type, mass-nature, anomaly, CP-existence all *are* such class functions; **masses, mixing angles, and the CP magnitude are not** (they distinguish members within a class), so I₁ provably *cannot* read them. The criterion is what makes "structure not spectrum" a theorem rather than a hope — it predicts exactly which observables the census is blind to.
- **I₂ (readability criterion — under construction, Lane D):** a fact is readable off the boundary-orientability iff it is a **ℤ₂ / Pin-cobordism invariant** of the Shilov boundary. Candidates it should reach: parity, ν_R-absence (banked); and — to test — the arrow of time, baryon-number/record immutability. Grace + Elie are building the I₂ criterion to the completeness of the I₁ one.

## The information bound (≈ 4.75 + 1 bits)

The reality-type census is **three blocks, each carrying one of three reality-types**, so its information content is **log₂(3³) = log₂ 27 ≈ 4.755 bits**. Orientability is **one further bit** (orientable / non-orientable). **So the entire *discrete internal structure* of the Standard Model — its gauge dimensions, its chirality, its anomaly-freedom, its neutrino nature, its CP-existence, its custodial symmetry — is under six bits of information**, generated by two geometric invariants of one domain. *(Striking coincidence, flagged not banked, per the three-different-Ns discipline: the census's 27 = 3³ equals N_c³ = 27, the fermionic-record value; whether the "three blocks" and "three colors" are the same three is a candidate, not a claim.)*

## Why this is #66, landed

Casey's forcing criterion for the minimal generating set: **necessity = linear independence** (no component droppable), **sufficiency = spanning** (every feature reached), **uniqueness = classification**. The two-invariant theorem is exactly that for the internal sector: I₁ and I₂ are independent (rep-type vs boundary-topology), spanning (every structural fact in the table), and the classification is *proved two* — not one (chirality/Majorana need I₂), not three (nothing escapes I₁ ∧ I₂). "The internal SM is one object read two ways" is now a theorem with a generator count.
